countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

In India the degree is regulated by the Council of Architecture, and entry is tied to a prescribed aptitude test in addition to school-leaving results.

universities.name: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
universities.summary: SRM Institute of Science and Technology is a private deemed-to-be university at Kattankulathur in Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu, about 45 minutes by road from Chennai airport. This record covers the Kattankulathur campus only, where international applicants can enter English-taught engineering, architecture, management, computing, science and commerce degrees.
universities.campusLifestyle: Kattankulathur is the founding campus, opened in 1985 as SRM Engineering College and now the headquarters of a deemed-to-be university that reports more than 60,000 full-time students across all its campuses. In the engineering data SRMIST submitted for India Rankings 2025 the faculty alone recorded 20,642 undergraduate, 586 postgraduate and 418 integrated-master's students, of whom 646, 25 and 5 respectively came from outside India, taught by 1,661 faculty members. The campus carries site-wide high-speed Wi-Fi, three banks and more than five ATMs, a food court and shops beyond the university canteen, separate gyms for men and women, and an on-site SRM Hotel used by visiting families.
universities.cityProfile: Kattankulathur sits on the GST Road in Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu, with the campus postal code 603203. SRMIST describes it as roughly a 45-minute drive from Chennai airport, reached from the city either by car or on the suburban electric train line that serves the campus. The surrounding corridor is one of the Chennai region's main industrial and IT belts, which is why several Kattankulathur programmes are run with named industry partners. The climate is tropical and matters for arrival planning: SRMIST describes moderate to heavy rain from October to December, a mild winter in January and February, a hot and humid summer from March to June that can reach about 104 degrees Fahrenheit, and warm weather with occasional rain from July to September. Because odd-semester classes start in July or August depending on faculty, most new international students arrive in the warm, showery part of the year rather than during the north-east monsoon.
universities.practicalExposure: Kattankulathur runs a Directorate of Career Centre from Tech Tower II that handles pre-placement talks, written tests, group discussions and interviews for all six faculties. The clearest verified outcome data is the engineering return SRMIST filed with the Ministry of Education for India Rankings 2025: of the 4,552 undergraduates who completed the four-year programme in the minimum stipulated time in 2023-24, 4,210 were placed and 212 went on to higher study, at a median salary of INR 620,000 per annum; at postgraduate level 278 of 297 completers were placed at a median of INR 612,000. The comparable 2022-23 undergraduate median was INR 610,000 and the 2021-22 median INR 449,000. Several Kattankulathur programmes are taught with a named partner rather than in the abstract: the B.Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems track runs in partnership with Tata Consultancy Services, M.Tech. Electric Vehicle Technology with Valeo, M.Tech. Information Security and Cyber Forensics with K7 Computing, the B.Tech. Automobile Engineering vehicles-testing stream with the Global Automotive Research Centre, and the MBA in Financial Services with the National Stock Exchange. The same India Rankings return records 106 sponsored research projects and 130 consultancy projects in 2023-24, and 821 full-time doctoral students.
universities.hostelOverview: Two air-conditioned blocks with a combined capacity of about 400 are reserved for international students: the NRI Premium International Hostel on campus, and the Green Pearl International Hostel about ten minutes' walk away with shuttle buses to campus. Published 2026-27 rates include mess and cover the June-to-March academic year. For men, N Block is INR 273,000 a year for an air-conditioned two-share room and INR 253,000 for three-share, Green Pearl B Block is INR 197,500 non-air-conditioned three-share or USD 3,500 for the off-campus air-conditioned option, and Began Block is INR 133,000 for a non-attached two-share room. For women, Kopperundevi ranges from INR 165,000 to INR 270,000 and Meenakshi from INR 213,000 to INR 233,000. Laundry is optional at INR 7,500 to INR 8,500.
universities.dietarySupport: Hostel fees include mess catering, so food is bundled into the room rate rather than billed separately. The Green Pearl International Hostel runs a multi-cuisine dining facility serving Thai, Chinese and Indian food. On campus there is a food court and several shops beyond the university canteen. Fridges, washing machines, microwaves, room heaters, irons, air coolers and kettles are barred from every hostel, so in-room self-catering is not an option.
universities.safetyOverview: The campus houses the SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre with over 1,500 beds and the SRM Global Hospital, both open in an emergency, and SRMIST recommends taking out medical insurance. An anti-ragging committee, an equal opportunity cell and a grievance redressal mechanism are standing committees. A student may move into an allotted hostel room only once admission formalities, the student visa and immigration are complete.
universities.studentSupport: The Office of International Relations works from the second floor of the Central Library Building, west wing. It handles Form C residential registration on campus for foreign nationals and OCI card holders, arranges Chennai airport transfers on prior request at the student's cost, issues visa letters, bonafide certificates and Aadhaar applications, and runs separate student-services and helpdesk mailboxes.
whyChoose: International applicants are admitted on qualifying-examination merit through the Directorate of International Relations, so no SRMJEEE entrance test applies to foreign, NRI, PIO and OCI candidates in the 2026 cycle

Both international fee tables are published in full: the Foreign table for 2026 and the NRI, PIO and OCI table for 2025 with its scholarship column, so an applicant can compare the two routes before applying

Kattankulathur holds accreditation and approval from several named bodies, including NAAC at A++ with a CGPA of 3.58 in its fourth cycle declared in June 2024, AICTE approval for 2025-26, and Council of Architecture approval for B.Arch. and M.Arch.

faq.question: Is SRM Institute of Science and Technology a public or a private university?
faq.answer: It is private. It began in 1985 as SRM Engineering College at Kattankulathur and was declared a deemed to be university under Section 3 of the UGC Act 1956 with effect from 2 August 2002. The University Grants Commission's list of deemed to be universities carries it as entry 112 for Tamil Nadu, with Kattankulathur as the main campus and Ramapuram, Vadapalani and Modinagar as further campuses.

faq.question: Which campus does this page cover, and does it matter?
faq.answer: This page covers the Kattankulathur campus in Chengalpattu district only. It matters because SRMIST's own international fee tables mix campuses in one list, marking rows KTR for Kattankulathur, RMP for Ramapuram and VDP for Vadapalani, and because some programmes and accreditations exist at one campus and not another. The Council of Architecture approvals and the ABET listing quoted here are the Kattankulathur ones.

faq.question: What language are the programmes taught in?
faq.answer: English. SRMIST states that the medium of instruction for all its programmes is English, with no transition to a local language later in the degree. Additional languages are taught as subjects rather than as the medium: the engineering stream offers French, Japanese, German, Chinese, Korean or Spanish, and the Science and Humanities and Management streams offer Tamil, Hindi or French.

faq.question: Do international applicants have to sit SRMJEEE or another entrance exam?
faq.answer: For most programmes, no. SRMIST states that there is no entrance examination for foreign, NRI, PIO and OCI candidates, and that undergraduate admission is decided on the marks obtained in the qualifying 10+2 or equivalent examination on a first-come, first-served basis, provided the eligibility requirements are met. The exception is B.Arch., which requires a NATA pass or, per SRMIST, a JEE (Main) Paper 2 result.

faq.question: What does an undergraduate year actually cost, beyond the headline tuition?
faq.answer: Take a 2026 B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering place at Kattankulathur as the worked example: USD 12,500 annual tuition, a one-time registration fee of USD 300, examination fees as announced each semester, and hostel with mess from about INR 133,000 to INR 273,000 a year depending on block and room type. Books, materials and transport are extra and are paid in Indian rupees. Cheaper programmes exist on the same campus, with most B.Tech. branches at USD 7,000 and the general B.Com. at USD 3,500.

faq.question: How do I apply, and what does it cost to apply?
faq.answer: Applications go to the SRMIST Directorate of International Relations through the international application form linked from the Admission International pages, not through the domestic admission portal. The application fee is USD 50 or INR 3,000, payable by credit card, debit card or net banking, and is non-refundable. SRMIST states that applications open in the first week of November each year.

faq.question: Is an English-language test such as IELTS or TOEFL required?
faq.answer: SRMIST does not publish an IELTS or TOEFL requirement on its international admission pages for the programmes covered here, and does not list one among the documents required at application or registration. Because a language-test rule can be added by an individual faculty, an applicant whose schooling was not in English should confirm the position with the Directorate of International Relations before paying the application fee.

faq.question: What is the difference between the Foreign and the NRI, PIO or OCI route?
faq.answer: They are separate admission categories with separate fee tables. The Foreign table publishes 2026 annual tuition with no scholarship column. The NRI, PIO and OCI table publishes the same annual figures for 2025 plus a scholarship column: a 40 per cent tuition waiver on engineering programmes and 50 per cent on others where the candidate meets the SAT score of 1000 out of 1600 or scores 70 per cent and above in the relevant higher-secondary subjects. SRMIST states no scholarship applies to the NRI Sponsored category, and that a candidate may apply in one category only.

faq.question: Who counts as a sponsor under the NRI Sponsored category?
faq.answer: SRMIST states that grandparents, parents and direct siblings of a candidate with NRI status are eligible to sponsor. It also states that a candidate who took the Grade 11 and Grade 12 examinations outside India must apply under the NRI category even if the school followed an Indian board, while a candidate who took those examinations inside India may choose either the domestic or the NRI-sponsored category, but not both.

faq.question: When do classes start and when does the application close?
faq.answer: The 2026 international deadline published for all courses is 30 August 2026, with PhD applications closing 30 April 2026 for the June intake and 30 October 2026 for the January intake. First-year start dates differ by faculty in 2026-27: engineering, architecture and design first-year classes begin on 17 August 2026 after orientation from 10 to 14 August, MBA first-year classes on 12 August 2026, and Science and Humanities first-year classes on 8 July 2026.

faq.question: What accreditation does the university hold, and what does it mean for a degree taken abroad?
faq.answer: SRMIST holds deemed-to-be-university status from the University Grants Commission and NAAC accreditation at the A++ grade with a CGPA of 3.58 in its fourth cycle, declared in June 2024. It also holds AICTE approval for its technical, management and computer-application programmes and Council of Architecture approval for B.Arch. and M.Arch. at Kattankulathur. Recognition of the resulting degree in another country is decided by that country's own credential-evaluation or licensing body, not by SRMIST, so the relevant authority in the destination country should be approached directly.

faq.question: What accommodation is available to international students and what does it cost?
faq.answer: Two air-conditioned blocks with a combined capacity of about 400 are set aside for international students: the NRI Premium International Hostel on campus and the Green Pearl International Hostel roughly ten minutes' walk away, with shuttle buses. Rooms are allotted on a first-come, first-served basis, and where international blocks are full SRMIST offers domestic hostel rooms subject to availability. Published 2026-27 rates run from INR 133,000 to INR 273,000 a year including mess, or USD 3,500 for the off-campus Green Pearl air-conditioned option.

faq.question: How does SRM Kattankulathur compare with other large private Indian universities on published outcomes?
faq.answer: The one comparison that rests on a common, government-collected dataset is the National Institutional Ranking Framework. In India Rankings 2025 the Ministry of Education placed S.R.M. Institute of Science and Technology 14th in the Engineering category with a score of 65.83 and 22nd in the Overall category with a score of 62.87. Rankings are a relative position rather than an accreditation, and they cover the institution as a whole rather than any individual programme on this page.

programmes.officialTitle: B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (Kattankulathur campus)

fee.notes: SRMIST publishes two separate tables for this programme at the Kattankulathur campus. The Foreign table gives an annual tuition fee of USD 12,500 for 2026. The NRI, PIO and OCI table gives the same USD 12,500 annual figure for 2025, alongside a column showing USD 7,500 after the 40 per cent engineering scholarship for candidates who meet the SAT or 70 per cent higher-secondary criteria; SRMIST states that no scholarship applies to the NRI Sponsored category. A one-time registration fee of USD 300 and examination fees apply on top, and the four-year total shown here is the annual figure multiplied by four rather than a published lump sum. Hostel, mess, books, materials and transport are billed separately and are payable in Indian rupees.

eligibleAudiences: Foreign nationals holding a valid passport, admitted through the SRMIST international admission category
NRI, PIO and OCI applicants, including the NRI Sponsored route where a grandparent, parent or direct sibling with NRI status sponsors the candidate
restrictions: The qualifying examination must be recognised by the Association of Indian Universities as equivalent to the Indian +2 stage, with an AIU eligibility certificate where required
A minimum 50 per cent aggregate in Physics, Mathematics and a prescribed third subject is required, with Physics and Mathematics compulsory
Candidates must have completed 17 years of age on or before 31 December of the admission year
Candidates who studied Grades 11 and 12 outside India must apply in the NRI or foreign category and not in the domestic category
SRMIST states that generally 15 per cent of total seats are set aside for the foreign and NRI quota, and that there is no management quota for international admissions

audienceEligibility.notes: SRMIST does not publish an IELTS or TOEFL requirement for this route; the medium of instruction for all programmes is English.

The 2026-27 calendar sets first-year postgraduate course enrolment on 29 June 2026 and the start of classes on 8 July 2026, with internal assessment I on 11 August 2026, internal assessment II on 21 September 2026, the model examination from 8 October 2026, the last working day on 16 October 2026 and university theory examinations from 2 November 2026. Even-semester classes for the same cohort begin on 30 November 2026. Related Kattankulathur postgraduate options in the same fee table include M.Sc. Computer Science, M.Sc. Information Technology and MCA.

fee.notes: The SRMIST Foreign fee table for Science and Humanities gives an annual tuition fee of USD 3,500 for the three-year general B.Com. at Kattankulathur in 2026, the same rate as the Accounting and Finance, Corporate Secretaryship and Computer Applications streams; the honours streams in International Accounting and Finance, Professional Accounting, Strategic Finance and Banking, Financial Services and Insurance are priced at USD 4,000. The NRI, PIO and OCI route carries a 50 per cent tuition waiver for non-engineering programmes where the SAT or 70 per cent higher-secondary criteria are met, which SRMIST states does not apply to the NRI Sponsored category. A one-time registration fee of USD 300 and examination fees apply separately, and the three-year total shown here is the annual figure multiplied by three.

eligibleAudiences: Foreign nationals holding a valid passport who studied Commerce and Accountancy at the +2 stage
NRI, PIO and OCI applicants who studied Commerce and Accountancy at the +2 stage, including the NRI Sponsored route
restrictions: The 10+2 higher secondary examination must include Commerce and Accountancy; applicants from a science or arts stream are directed to the Information System and Management stream of the B.Com. instead
A minimum aggregate of 50 per cent in the qualifying examination is required
The qualifying board must be recognised by the Association of Indian Universities as equivalent to the Indian +2 stage, with an AIU eligibility certificate where required
Applicants who studied Grades 11 and 12 outside India must apply in the NRI or foreign category and cannot apply in the domestic category
The 50 per cent scholarship band published for commerce applicants is assessed on Accounts, Commerce and Economics results and excludes marks in language subjects
audienceEligibility.notes: Subject prerequisites differ between B.Com. streams at the same campus, so the stream chosen on the application form determines whether a non-commerce +2 profile is eligible.

admissionsContent.overview: International applicants apply to the SRMIST Directorate of International Relations for a place in the Faculty of Science and Humanities at Kattankulathur. Entry rests on the +2 subject combination and a minimum 50 per cent aggregate, and the offer is confirmed once the first-year fees are received.

eligibility.intro: Entry needs a school-leaving qualification recognised as equivalent to the Indian +2 stage, taken with commerce subjects, and assessed against Association of Indian Universities norms for foreign awards.
items: A pass in the 10+2 higher secondary examination or a recognised equivalent with Commerce and Accountancy as subjects
A minimum aggregate of 50 per cent in the qualifying examination
The qualifying board must be recognised by the Association of Indian Universities as equivalent to the Indian +2 stage, with an AIU eligibility certificate where required
Applicants who studied Grades 11 and 12 outside India must apply in the NRI or foreign category and cannot apply in the domestic category
For scholarship assessment, CBSE applicants are scored on their overall percentage and applicants from other boards on any three qualifying subjects, with language subjects excluded

applicationSteps: Apply online through the SRMIST international application and pay the non-refundable application fee of USD 50 or INR 3,000 by credit card, debit card or net banking
Complete every field of the form; where a result is still pending, enter 'Results are awaited' and send the actual marksheet to the Directorate of International Relations as soon as it is issued
Upload the qualifying transcripts with both sides of each marksheet, plus a certified English translation of any document not issued in English
Receive the application number allotted by email and quote it in all later correspondence with the Directorate of International Relations
On meeting the eligibility criteria, receive the provisional admission letter by email with the tuition and other fees payable; SRMIST states this letter is not valid for visa purposes

Pay the annual tuition, one-time registration and examination fees in US dollars by electronic transfer within 10 days of the provisional letter, exclusive of bank charges, then email the electronic fund transfer details to ir.accounts@srmist.edu.in
Receive the confirmed admission letter once the first-year fees and final marksheets are in; SRMIST states this letter may be used to apply for the student visa, ticketing and insurance
Arrive at Kattankulathur two to three days before classes begin and complete pre-enrolment and registration at the Office of International Relations

academic: Grade 10 and Grade 12 certificates with marksheets or transcripts, copied on both front and back
Certified English translation of any certificate or marksheet not issued in English
Predicted, forecast or term results endorsed by the head of school where final results are pending
Association of Indian Universities equivalence certificate where the qualifying board requires one
Migration certificate where applicable, and the transfer or school-leaving certificate from the last institution
Degree or pass certificate and grade sheet of the qualifying examination, produced in original at registration
application: Copy of the applicant's passport, personal details page
Copy of the passport of the parent or sponsor, personal details page
Proof of NRI status of the student, parent or sponsor for NRI-category applicants
Passport carrying a valid student visa, produced in original at registration
Fifteen recent passport-size photographs for the various departments
Declaration forms completed and signed by the parent, required by the local government

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - official site
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: The UGC publishes a list of fake universities alongside its lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, so institutional recognition must be checked against UGC records before an Indian institution is presented as degree-awarding.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission - Higher Education Institutions listings
evidence.internalNotes: Operational rule for this catalogue: no Indian university is published without a verifiable UGC listing and, where applicable, AICTE approval or NMC recognition.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
evidence.internalNotes: General climatic framing only; do not present city-level weather claims at country level.

evidence.claimText: SRM Institute of Science and Technology is listed by the University Grants Commission as a deemed to be university under Section 3 of the UGC Act 1956, in Tamil Nadu, with effect from 02-08-2002 and with Kattankulathur named as its main campus.
evidence.sourceLabel: UGC - List of Deemed to be Universities
evidence.internalNotes: Entry 112 of the UGC deemed-university list. Corroborated by the SRMIST history page, which records the 2002 declaration, and by the SRMIST academic calendars, which carry the 'Deemed to be University u/s 3 of UGC Act, 1956' subtitle.

evidence.claimText: The Kattankulathur campus is located at SRM Nagar, Kattankulathur 603203, Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu, and SRMIST describes it as around a 45-minute drive from Chennai airport.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - FAQs, International Admissions 2025-2026
evidence.internalNotes: Address corroborated on the Faculty of Science and Humanities academic calendar 2026-27 header and on the Directorate of International Relations contact block.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST began in 1985 as SRM Engineering College at Kattankulathur, near Chennai, and was granted university status in 2002.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - About us and History
evidence.internalNotes: The About page gives 'Established 1985 - SRMIST' and the history timeline gives the 1985 launch of SRM Engineering College and the 2002 UGC deemed-status declaration. Corroborated by the international FAQ document.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST reports over 60,000 full-time students and more than 4,460 faculty across all campuses, offering programmes in six faculties: Engineering and Technology, Management, Medicine and Health Sciences, Science and Humanities, Law and Agricultural Sciences.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - About us
evidence.internalNotes: Institution-reported group-wide figure covering all campuses, not Kattankulathur alone; the page copy attributes it to the university as a whole and it is presented that way.

evidence.claimText: In the engineering data submitted for India Rankings 2025, SRMIST recorded 20,642 undergraduate, 586 postgraduate and 418 integrated-master's students, including 646, 25 and 5 respectively from outside the country, and entered 1,661 faculty members.
evidence.sourceLabel: NIRF India Rankings 2025 - Engineering data submitted by the institution (IR-E-U-0473)
evidence.internalNotes: Government-hosted institutional return under IR-E-U-0473. Covers the engineering submission only, which is how it is described in the public copy.

evidence.claimText: The campus has site-wide high-speed Wi-Fi, three banks and more than five ATMs, a food court and shops in addition to the university canteen, separate gyms for male and female students, and an SRM Hotel on the campus site.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - Admissions International, Engineering and Technology
evidence.internalNotes: Wi-Fi and SRM Hotel details corroborated in the international FAQ document.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST describes the local climate as moderate to heavy rain from October to December, a mild winter in January and February, hot and humid weather from March to June reaching about 104 degrees Fahrenheit, and warm weather with occasional rain from July to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - FAQs, International Admissions 2025-2026
evidence.internalNotes: Consistent with the India country-level climate note sourced from the India Meteorological Department.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST states that the campus is reached from Chennai city by car or local electric train, and that Chennai must be reached first by road, rail or air.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - FAQs, International Admissions 2025-2026

evidence.claimText: Of the 4,552 undergraduate engineering students who graduated in the minimum stipulated time in 2023-24, SRMIST reported 4,210 placed at a median salary of INR 620,000 per annum and 212 selected for higher studies; at postgraduate level 278 of 297 completers were placed at a median of INR 612,000.
evidence.sourceLabel: NIRF India Rankings 2025 - Engineering data submitted by the institution (IR-E-U-0473)
evidence.internalNotes: The same return gives 2022-23 and 2021-22 undergraduate medians of INR 610,000 and INR 449,000. The SRMIST placements page renders its own counters through JavaScript and returned no readable figures, so only the government-hosted return is used.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST reported 106 sponsored research projects and 130 consultancy projects in 2023-24, and 821 full-time doctoral students up to 2023-24.
evidence.sourceLabel: NIRF India Rankings 2025 - Engineering data submitted by the institution (IR-E-U-0473)

evidence.claimText: SRMIST lists Kattankulathur programmes run with named partners, including B.Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems with Tata Consultancy Services, M.Tech. Electric Vehicle Technology with Valeo, M.Tech. Information Security and Cyber Forensics with K7 Computing, B.Tech. Automobile Engineering with Vehicles Testing at the Global Automotive Research Centre, and an MBA in Financial Services with the National Stock Exchange.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - Admissions International, Engineering and Technology
evidence.internalNotes: The MBA with the National Stock Exchange appears on the Faculty of Management academic calendar and the management international fee table; the remainder appear as programme names in the engineering international fee tables.

evidence.claimText: Published 2026-27 hostel rates including mess at Kattankulathur run from INR 133,000 for a non-attached two-share room in Began Block to INR 273,000 for an air-conditioned two-share room in N Block for men, and from INR 148,000 to INR 270,000 for women, with an off-campus air-conditioned Green Pearl option at USD 3,500 and optional laundry at INR 7,500 to INR 8,500.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - Admissions International, Engineering and Technology
evidence.internalNotes: Taken from the Girls Hostel Booking 2026-27 and Boys Hostel Booking 2026-27 tables. The same page states that hostel fees include the mess and that the hostel payment period runs from June to March.

evidence.claimText: Two air-conditioned blocks with a combined capacity of around 400 are allotted to international students: the NRI Premium International Hostel on campus and the Green Pearl International Hostel outside the campus, about ten minutes' walk away, with shuttle buses to campus.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - International Hostel
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated in the international FAQ document, which adds that international rooms are limited and that domestic hostel rooms are offered to the remaining students subject to availability.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST states that hostel fees include the mess, that the Green Pearl International Hostel offers multi-cuisine dining with Thai, Chinese and Indian food, and that fridges, washing machines, microwaves, room heaters, irons, air coolers and kettles are not allowed in any hostel.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - International Hostel
evidence.internalNotes: The prohibited-appliance list and the food court are stated in the international FAQ document and the engineering international admissions page respectively.

evidence.claimText: The Kattankulathur campus houses the SRM Medical College and Research Centre with over 1,500 beds and the SRM Global Hospital, both available in an emergency, and SRMIST recommends obtaining a medical insurance policy.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - FAQs, International Admissions 2025-2026
evidence.internalNotes: The engineering international admissions page states separately that SRM General Hospital and SRM Global Corporate Hospitals are available for medical emergencies.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST states that a student is permitted to move into the allotted hostel only after completing admission formalities, document verification, the student visa and the immigration process.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - FAQs, International Admissions 2025-2026
evidence.internalNotes: Anti-ragging, anti-discrimination, equal opportunity and grievance redressal committees are published as standing committees in the SRMIST site navigation.

evidence.claimText: The Office of International Relations, on the second floor of the Central Library Building west wing, handles Form C residential registration on campus for foreign nationals and OCI holders, arranges airport transfers on prior request at the student's cost, and issues visa letters, bonafide certificates and Aadhaar applications.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - International Admission Details, Directorate of International Relations

evidence.claimText: NAAC records SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Kattankulathur as accredited at the A++ grade with a CGPA of 3.58 in Cycle 4, declared on 16 June 2024.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - Accreditation status, institutions with valid accreditation
evidence.internalNotes: Confirmed against the NAAC workbook 'Institutions accredited by NAAC having valid accreditation as on 14-08-2025' (Universities sheet, AISHE U-0473, Tamil Nadu) and corroborated against the 203rd Standing Committee result of 16 June 2024. The workbook publishes a date of declaration and no expiry date, so the badge states the declaration year only and makes no valid-to claim; SRMIST's own page asserts a 15 June 2031 end date that the regulator does not publish.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST publishes AICTE approval for the Kattankulathur campus for the academic year 2025-26, covering engineering and technology, design, MBA, BBA, MCA and BCA programmes with an approved total intake of 30,967 across all campuses and modes.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - Statutory and Regulatory Authority Approvals 2025-26
evidence.internalNotes: The disclosure links to the AICTE sanction letter for the Kattankulathur campus. AICTE's own portal was not queried; the claim is limited to the fact of approval as disclosed.

evidence.claimText: The Council of Architecture approved B.Arch. with an intake of 80 and M.Arch. Architectural Design with an intake of 20 at the Kattankulathur campus for 2025-26.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - Statutory and Regulatory Authority Approvals 2025-26

evidence.claimText: The National Board of Accreditation register records no current accreditation for SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Kattankulathur.
evidence.sourceLabel: NBA - Accreditation programme registers
evidence.internalNotes: Checked against all nine NBA registers. The only SRM IST entity present is SRM Engineering College, a constituent unit of SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Chennai, in the Tier II register, with accreditation periods of 5 years from 21-02-1998, 3 years from 01-04-2001 and 5 years from 24-04-2002, all expired by 2007. SRM Valliammai Engineering College and SRM TRP Engineering College hold current accreditations but are separate colleges and must not be borrowed. SRMIST's own accreditations page asserts NBA programme accreditation to 30 June 2027 or 2028; that assertion is not supported by the register and has been removed from the badges, the FAQ, the whyChoose list and the Mechanical, Civil and Electronics and Communication teaching-phase notes. Do not re-add without a fresh register check.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST lists B.Tech. Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering and Electronics and Communication Engineering at Kattankulathur as accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - Accreditations and Rankings
evidence.internalNotes: OPEN ITEM, still unresolved at 2026-08-22: the ABET accredited-programme search at amspub.abet.org is a JavaScript application and returned no data to an automated request. A follow-up regulator verification pass with browser tooling resolved the NAAC, NBA, BCI and UGC IoE portals but did not settle ABET, so this badge stays indicative and flagged. Note also that the SRMIST international FAQ gives a different list, naming ECE, EEE, Mechanical, Civil and IT, while the accreditations page names Civil, Mechanical, EEE and ECE; the accreditations page list is used because it is the more recently maintained source, and the conflict is itself a reason to re-verify against ABET.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST's Institution of Engineering and Technology accreditation for four Kattankulathur B.Tech. programmes is stated as running only until 2022.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - Accreditations and Rankings
evidence.internalNotes: Deliberately excluded from recognitionBadges because the stated validity has lapsed. Recorded so that a later reviewer does not add it back.

evidence.claimText: The Bar Council of India approved list of Centres of Legal Education records SRM School of Law, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu with a 5-year B.Com. LL.B. (Hons.) approved up to the academic year 2025-26, a 3-year LL.B. of 120 places approved up to 2024-25 and a third course approved up to 2015-16.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bar Council of India - Recognised universities and colleges, approved list of Centres of Legal Education
evidence.internalNotes: No law programme is packaged in this record, and none should be added on this evidence: the newest BCI approval window ends with the academic year 2025-26 and is therefore lapsed or awaiting renewal at the checked date. If a later agent packages SRM law programmes, re-check the next BCI upload of the approved-CLE list first. Note also that BCI approves LL.B.-track undergraduate law courses only and does not accredit LL.M. programmes, so no BCI claim can attach to a postgraduate law offering.

evidence.claimText: SRM Institute of Science and Technology does not appear on the UGC list of Institutions of Eminence, which names twelve notified institutions across its public and private tables.
evidence.sourceLabel: UGC - List of Institutions of Eminence
evidence.internalNotes: Checked directly against the UGC IoE list route. SRMIST asserts no Institution of Eminence status of its own, and none is claimed anywhere in this payload. Recorded so the absence is a verified negative finding rather than an untested gap.

evidence.claimText: In India Rankings 2025 the Ministry of Education placed S.R.M. Institute of Science and Technology 14th in the Engineering category with a score of 65.83.
evidence.sourceLabel: NIRF India Rankings 2025 - Engineering ranking table
evidence.internalNotes: Kept out of recognitionBadges because a ranking position is not an accreditation.

evidence.claimText: In India Rankings 2025 the Ministry of Education placed S.R.M. Institute of Science and Technology 22nd in the Overall category with a score of 62.87.
evidence.sourceLabel: NIRF India Rankings 2025 - Overall ranking table
evidence.internalNotes: Kept out of recognitionBadges because a ranking position is not an accreditation. SRMIST's own pages additionally quote a UI GreenMetric position and an ARIIA 2020 position; those are awards or sustainability ratings and are not reproduced.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST states that the medium of instruction for all its programmes is English, and that foreign languages are offered as taught subjects: French, Japanese, German, Chinese, Korean or Spanish for engineering, and Tamil, Hindi or French for Science and Humanities and Management.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - FAQs, International Admissions 2025-2026

evidence.claimText: SRMIST states that there is no entrance examination for foreign, NRI, PIO and OCI candidates and that undergraduate admission is on merit in the qualifying examination on a first-come, first-served basis, and separately that there is no management quota for international admissions and that generally 15 per cent of total seats are reserved for the foreign and NRI quota.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - FAQs, International Admissions 2025-2026
evidence.internalNotes: The engineering international admissions page corroborates the merit-cum-first-come-first-served confirmation rule.

evidence.claimText: SRMIST states that grandparents, parents and direct siblings of a candidate with NRI status may sponsor under the NRI Sponsored category, and that a candidate who took Grades 11 and 12 outside India must apply under the NRI category rather than the domestic category.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - FAQs, International Admissions 2025-2026

evidence.claimText: SRMIST states that tuition, hostel, registration, examination and other applicable fees must be paid in US dollars by electronic transfer within 10 days of the provisional admission letter, exclusive of bank charges, that cash and cheques are not accepted, and that the provisional admission letter is not valid for visa purposes.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRMIST - Admissions International, Engineering and Technology
